inputs.text: This talk of Cuba “heading toward” a transition sounds less like concern for ordinary people and more like setting the stage for a managed sell-off. If residents own nothing and are too impoverished to buy the businesses still operating, that isn’t just an unfortunate side effect—it leaves them unable to compete while wealthy outsiders wait for bargain prices. The language of transition may be preparing people to accept a transfer of property away from Cubans and into the hands of the diaspora and foreign investors.

output.main_topic: The possibility that transition rhetoric about Cuba could facilitate a property sell-off disadvantaging residents
subtopics: Residents' lack of property and ability to buy businesses
Wealthy outsiders waiting for bargain prices
